newsitem.title: ROMANIA: World Bank lends Romania $70 mln for education.
newsitem.headline: World Bank lends Romania $70 mln for education.

text.p: The World Bank said on Wednesday it had approved a $70 million loan for Romania to upgrade schools in rural areas and fight poverty.

"..(The project) will repair about 900 seriously damaged pre-university schools, mostly in rural areas, in support of the government's education reform programme," it said in a statement from its Washington headquarters.
It said the bank was funding 66 percent of the total cost of the project estimated at $130 million.
Romania's government and the Council of Europe Social Development Fund will provide the rest. The 20-year loan, with a grace period of five years, bears the standard World Bank interest rate.
The World Bank had previously backed education reforms in Romania with loans totalling $100 million in 1994 and 1996.
Last month, the World Bank unlocked a $80 million tranche of a $280 million Financial and Enterprise Structural Adjustment Loan (FESAL).
Its board earlier approved about $550 million in other credits to support the Romanian farm sector, underpin social benefits and upgrade potholed roads.
The final $100 million tranche of the FESAL credit is subject to the government meeting a series of targets, probably within the next 12 months.
